Frequently Asked Questions

Question: Do you know which bin string lights go in?
Answer: String lights have to go to an electronics drop-off or a store take-back program.

Question: When should I book bulky pickup before moving?
Answer: Book bulky item pickup well before moving day, or ask the property manager about the bulky item area.

Question: Where do ceramic dishes belong?
Answer: Ceramic dishes are garbage and go in the black cart. If they are still in good condition, donate them instead. Wrap sharp pieces in newspaper first. Drinking glasses, window glass, mirrors and ovenware are not recyclable; wrap them and put them in the garbage.

Question: How do I keep my compost pile healthy?
Answer: Balance wet greens with dry browns like leaves and turn the compost from time to time.

Question: Can wrong items in carts hurt workers?
Answer: Wrong items, especially batteries and plastic bags, can damage equipment, start fires and injure workers.

Subject: Resident questions about air conditioners, frozen food bags, aluminum trays, printers

Hello everyone,

Regards,

Team,

A-Z Sorting Guide

Broken glass - black garbage cart. Wrap it carefully so no one gets cut.
See also: glass shards, broken window glass

Cat litter - garbage (black cart). Always bag it.
See also: kitty litter, used litter

Diapers - black cart. Bag them and tie the bag closed. Diapers are not compostable even if they are labelled that way.

Lithium-ion batteries - household hazardous waste drop-off. Cover the terminals with clear tape. Lithium-ion batteries are a leading cause of fires in collection trucks.
Includes: rechargeable batteries, phone batteries, laptop batteries

Medications - pharmacy take-back program. Never flush medications or put them in the garbage.

Plastic bags - garbage (black cart). Plastic bags tangle sorting machines. Reuse them as long as you can, then put them in the garbage.
Also called: plastic grocery bags, shopping bags, produce bags

Plastic milk jugs - recycling (blue cart). Empty them out first. A quick rinse is enough; they do not need to be spotless. Leave the lid on.

Wrapping paper - blue recycling cart. It should be clean and dry. Plain wrapping paper is recyclable, but foil, glitter and metallic wrap go in the garbage. Ribbons and bows go in the garbage too.
Also called: gift wrap, tissue gift paper

Sorting Directory (excerpt)

Ceramic dishes: If you have ceramic dishes, they belong in the black garbage cart. Donation is the best option if they are still usable. Wrap sharp pieces in newspaper first.
Includes: plates, mugs, bowls

Holiday trees: The rule for holiday trees is simple: they belong in the green organics bin. Take off any decorations first. Cut or break them so they fit in the cart with the lid closed. Keep in mind: Trees can be cut to fit in the green cart or set out whole on the holiday tree collection days announced each winter. Artificial trees go in the garbage or to bulky item pickup.

Newspapers: Newspapers? They go into the blue recycling cart. Make sure they are dry; wet paper is hard to recycle. Place them loose in the cart, not in a bag.

Paper egg cartons: Residents often ask about paper egg cartons. They are accepted in the blue recycling cart. Empty them out first. They should be clean and dry. Foam egg cartons are different and go in the garbage.
Also called: cardboard egg cartons

Pool chemicals: Residents often ask about pool chemicals. They should be dropped off at a household hazardous waste drop-off. Leave them in the original container with the label on. Do not combine them with other chemicals.

Sorting FAQ

Why did my cart get a tag?
Carts with the wrong items may be skipped and tagged with a note explaining why.

Is it okay to leave a mattress on the curb?
Putting bulky items at the curb without booking counts as illegal dumping.

Do leaves go in the green cart?
Yes. They count as organics and go in the green cart. Keep in mind: Extra leaves can be set out in paper yard waste bags beside the green cart. This is because they will break down into compost.

Where do I put large appliances when I am done with them?
They are collected as bulky waste once you book a pickup. Book a bulky item pickup in advance, or use your building's bulky item area. This is because they are too large to fit in a cart.

How do I dispose of margarine tubs?
The guide says margarine tubs are accepted in the blue recycling cart. Scrape any leftover food into the green organics cart. Rinse them with a little water. Screw the cap back on before recycling.

Is there anything I should do with newspapers first?
They go in the blue recycling cart. Make sure they are dry; wet paper is hard to recycle. Put them in loose; do not bag them.

Textile Basics

Wearable clothing should be donated. Worn-out textiles go to a textile drop-off bin, never the recycling cart.

Before you start:
- Donate wearable and usable items.
- Textiles must be clean, dry and in a tied bag.
- Worn-out or torn textiles go to a textile drop-off bin, not the recycling cart.

Item by item:
- Do not guess with clothing: it belongs in textile donation, not the recycling cart. Donation is the best option if it is still usable. Make sure it is clean and dry and bring it in a tied bag. Tip: Even torn or stained clothing can go to a textile drop-off bin. Why? Because textiles can be reused or turned into new fibres.
- If you have tablecloths, they belong in textile donation, not the recycling cart. Bag them and keep them dry.
- Bed sheets and towels go to a textile drop-off. Donation is the best option if they are still usable. Wash and dry them, then put them in a tied bag.
- Residents often ask about stuffed animals. They belong in textile donation, not the recycling cart. If they are still in good condition, donate them instead. Make sure they are clean and dry and bring them in a tied bag.
- If you have sneakers, they belong in textile donation, not the recycling cart. Consider donating them if they are in good shape. Tie pairs together. Wash and dry them, then put them in a tied bag.
- Handbags and belts: Donation is the best option if they are still usable. Wash and dry them, then put them in a tied bag.

Rule of thumb: Clothes and other fabric go to donation or a textile drop-off.

Organics Basics

Your green cart is for food scraps of every kind, greasy or dirty paper, and yard waste.

Before you start:
- No plastic of any kind, including bags labelled compostable.
- All food scraps are accepted, including meat, bones and dairy.
- Line the kitchen pail with newspaper or a paper bag if you want to.

Items residents ask about:
- Residents often ask about pumpkins. They belong in the green organics cart. Take off any decorations first. Remove candles and any paint or decorations.
- Fruit and vegetable scraps: Green cart.
- Dairy products: Leave the packaging out.
- Cut grass: Green cart.
- If you have houseplants and cut flowers, they count as organics and go in the green cart. Tip: Remove any plastic pot, wrapping or elastic bands first.
- Used paper napkins? They belong in the green cart.
- Fish scraps: Remove any plastic packaging first.

Remember: Once paper is greasy or covered in food, put it in the green cart.

Holiday trees are organics once fully undecorated.

Sorting by Material


1. If you can eat it, or it came from food, it goes in the green cart.
2. Rinse glass jars and bottles and put them in recycling.
3. Anything smaller than a credit card should not go loose in recycling. Think: plastic straws.
4. Anything with a plug, cord or battery is electronic waste and goes to an electronics drop-off.
5. Foam cannot be recycled, so put it in the garbage. Like: foam egg cartons, packing peanuts, foam takeout containers.
6. Chemicals with warning labels are household hazardous waste. Like: motor oil, paint thinner and solvents.
7. Garden waste belongs in organics.
8. Empty metal cans and clean foil are recyclable in the blue cart. Think: food cans.

Collection schedule: what residents need to know

Collection days differ by area, so look up your area's collection calendar in the app or on the website. Your green cart is emptied every week. Garbage and recycling take turns, each collected every second week. Have your carts at the curb by early morning on your collection day, or set them out the evening before. Once emptied, carts should be brought back from the curb the same day. In a week with a public holiday, collection may be delayed by one day; the area calendar shows any changes.

Common Questions About Waste in Tidewell

- Is there anything I should do with shoes first?
The guide says shoes go to a textile drop-off. If they are still in good condition, donate them instead. Tie the pairs so they stay matched. Bag them and keep them dry. Fabric items, worn or not, are collected at textile drop-off bins.

- Why was my recycling left with a note?
If a cart is contaminated, the crew may leave it with a warning tag.

- What is contamination?
Contamination means putting the wrong items in a cart, such as plastic bags in recycling or plastic in organics.

- How do I report a missed pickup?
Missed collections should be reported by the end of the next day through the website, app or customer service line.

- Can I put hair and pet fur in the green bin?
Yes. The guide says hair and pet fur can go in your green organics cart.

Reduce and reuse - the waste guide

The best way to reduce waste is to avoid it: buy only what you need and choose reusable bags, bottles and containers. Pass on things you no longer need instead of throwing them away. Plan meals and store food properly to cut down on food waste.

Paints, chemicals, fuels, batteries and mercury items are household hazardous waste and must be dropped off.
